prompt: Sodium propanoate heated with soda lime (NaOH + CaO) mainly gives which alkane?
explain: Decarboxylation removes one carbon as carbonate: C₂H₅COONa → C₂H₆.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: The Wurtz reaction is carried out in which medium?
explain: Na reacts with water, so dry ether is used.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Wurtz reaction with a mixture of CH₃Br and C₂H₅Br gives how many different alkanes?
explain: Ethane, propane and butane form (R–R, R–R′, R′–R′), so the mixture is hard to separate.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which alkane cannot be prepared by the Wurtz reaction?
explain: Wurtz couples two alkyl groups, so the product has at least two carbons.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Catalyst and temperature in the Sabatier–Senderens reduction of alkenes to alkanes:
explain: Alkene + H₂ over finely divided Ni at 200–300 °C gives the alkane.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Corey–House synthesis of alkanes uses which reagent with an alkyl halide?
explain: R₂CuLi couples with R′X, so unsymmetrical alkanes can be made cleanly.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Hydrolysis of a Grignard reagent RMgX with water gives:
explain: The carbanion-like R of RMgX takes H⁺ from water to form the alkane.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Alkyl halide heated with zinc in dry ether to give an alkane is called:
explain: The Frankland reaction is the Wurtz-type coupling with Zn in place of Na.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In the Wurtz reaction, tertiary alkyl halides mainly give:
explain: Tertiary halides undergo dehydrohalogenation with Na, so the yield of alkane is poor.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Kolbe electrolysis of aqueous potassium succinate gives mainly:
explain: Dicarboxylate salts give alkenes: (CH₂COOK)₂ → CH₂=CH₂ + 2CO₂.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Kolbe's electrolytic synthesis of alkanes proceeds through which intermediate?
explain: RCOO• loses CO₂ to give R•, and two R• radicals combine to form R–R.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Clemmensen reduction converts C=O of aldehydes/ketones to CH₂ using:
explain: Zn–Hg/conc. HCl reduces carbonyl to methylene, giving the alkane (Wolff–Kishner does it in basic medium).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Among pentane isomers, which has the lowest boiling point?
explain: Branching makes the molecule more spherical, so surface area and van der Waals forces fall. Neopentane boils at about 9.5 °C.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Why is direct iodination of alkanes by I₂ not feasible?
options: The reaction is reversible; HI reduces R–I
explain: HI reduces R–I back to R–H. It works only if HI is removed by an oxidising agent such as HIO₃ or HNO₃.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which halogen is most selective in free-radical substitution of alkanes?
explain: Br· is less reactive and abstracts H with a late transition state. It prefers 3° over 2° over 1° H far more than Cl· does.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: n-Hexane over Cr₂O₃–Al₂O₃ at 773 K and 10–20 atm gives which product?
explain: This is aromatization: cyclisation followed by dehydrogenation, so n-hexane gives benzene.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: n-Butane with anhydrous AlCl₃/HCl undergoes which reaction?
explain: Anhydrous AlCl₃ with HCl isomerises n-alkanes to branched alkanes, so n-butane gives 2-methylpropane.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Methane and O₂ (9:1) passed through a Cu tube at 523 K and 100 atm give mainly:
explain: Controlled oxidation with Cu as catalyst gives methanol. With Mo₂O₃ the product is HCHO.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Oxidation of isobutane with KMnO₄ gives mainly:
explain: The tertiary C–H bond is oxidised selectively, so a 3° alkane gives a 3° alcohol.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Steam reforming of methane (Ni, 1273 K) gives which products?
explain: Ni catalyses CH₄ + H₂O → CO + 3H₂, which is water gas or synthesis gas, a source of H₂.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Dihedral angle between C–H bonds of adjacent carbons in eclipsed ethane?
explain: In the eclipsed form each front C–H lies exactly behind a rear C–H, so the dihedral angle is 0°.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Dihedral angle between nearest H atoms on adjacent carbons in staggered ethane?
explain: Staggered: each rear H lies midway between two front H atoms, giving a 60° dihedral angle.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Why is eclipsed ethane less stable than staggered?
explain: Eclipsed C–H bonds repel each other (torsional strain); bond angles stay about 109.5°.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In a Newman projection, the rear carbon is represented by:
options: The point where three bonds meet
explain: Front carbon = intersection of three bonds (centre); rear carbon = circle, with its bonds drawn from the circle's edge.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: A Newman projection of ethane is obtained by viewing the molecule:
options: Obliquely from above and the side
explain: Newman projection is an end-on view along the C–C bond; the sawhorse is an oblique view.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Sawhorse projection of ethane shows the C–C bond viewed:
options: In the plane as a dash only
explain: Sawhorse: C–C drawn as a slanting line viewed obliquely, each carbon bearing three bonds.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Ethane conformers cannot be separated at room temperature because:
options: Rotation barrier is very low (~12 kJ/mol)
C–C bond is a π bond
explain: The tiny barrier lets C–C rotate freely at room temperature, so conformers interconvert rapidly.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Conformations of ethane arise due to rotation about which bond?
explain: Free rotation about the C–C single (σ) bond generates the different spatial arrangements.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of eclipsed and staggered maxima/minima in one full 360° rotation of ethane?
explain: The energy curve repeats every 120°, giving 3 eclipsed (maxima) and 3 staggered (minima) forms.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Intermediate conformations of ethane between eclipsed and staggered are called:
explain: Any conformation other than perfectly staggered or eclipsed is a skew (twist) conformation.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of possible conformations of ethane theoretically:
explain: Rotation is continuous, so infinite conformations exist; staggered and eclipsed are the two extremes.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Conformers of ethane are classified as:
explain: Conformers have the same connectivity and differ only in spatial arrangement by rotation about single bonds.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In staggered ethane, the dihedral angle between H atoms on opposite sides (anti) is:
explain: Each H on the front carbon has an anti H on the rear carbon at 180°; the other two are at 60°.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Energy difference between eclipsed and staggered ethane is about:
explain: Eclipsed ethane is ~12.5 kJ/mol (≈3 kcal/mol) higher in energy than staggered; this is the torsional barrier.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Initiation step in photochemical chlorination of methane involves which process?
explain: hν splits Cl–Cl homolytically into two chlorine radicals, which starts the chain.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which propagation step regenerates Cl• in the chlorination of methane?
explain: The methyl radical abstracts Cl from Cl₂, giving the product and a new Cl• to continue the chain.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Trace ethane found in the chlorination of methane arises from which step?
explain: Two methyl radicals combine in a termination step to give C₂H₆.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Direct iodination of alkanes is reversible; which reagent is added to make it go forward?
explain: HI reduces R–I back to R–H. An oxidant like HIO₃ or HNO₃ removes HI by oxidising it to I₂.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Geometry and hybridisation of the methyl radical •CH₃ formed in propagation?
explain: The unpaired electron sits in a p orbital, so the radical is trigonal planar and sp² hybridised.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Radical halogenation at a stereocentre of an optically active alkane gives mainly?
explain: The planar radical is attacked by X₂ from either face with equal probability, giving a racemic mixture.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of monochloro structural isomers formed from 2-methylbutane by free-radical chlorination?

subject: Chemistry

prompt: Toluene with Cl₂/hν (or heat) gives mainly which product?

subject: Chemistry

prompt: A trace of which species inhibits the radical chain chlorination of alkanes?
explain: O₂ traps alkyl radicals (forming peroxy radicals) and terminates chains, so there is an induction period.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: CH₄ and Cl₂ are mixed in the dark at room temperature. What happens?
options: Explosive reaction gives C and HCl

subject: Chemistry

prompt: Alkyne + H₂ over Lindlar's catalyst gives which alkene?
explain: Poisoned Pd (Lindlar) gives syn addition of H₂, so the product is the cis-alkene.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Reduction of 2-butyne with Na in liquid NH₃ gives mainly:
explain: Dissolving-metal reduction involves anti addition of H, so it gives the trans-alkene.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Ease of acid-catalysed dehydration of alcohols follows the order:
explain: Dehydration goes via a carbocation (E1), and 3° carbocations are the most stable.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Ethanol heated with conc. H₂SO₄ gives ethene at which temperature?
explain: At 443 K ethene forms. At 413 K with excess alcohol, diethyl ether forms instead.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Vicinal dibromide on heating with Zn dust in ethanol gives:
explain: Dehalogenation: Zn removes two adjacent Br atoms to form C=C.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: How many geometrical isomers does CH₃–CH=CH–CH=CH–CH₃ have?
explain: The molecule is symmetric, so there are EE, ZZ and EZ (= ZE), giving 3 isomers.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In the Z-isomer of an alkene, the higher CIP priority groups are:

subject: Chemistry

prompt: Electrolysis of aqueous potassium succinate (Kolbe) gives:
explain: Kolbe electrolysis of a salt of a dicarboxylic acid (succinate) gives an alkene, here ethene.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Alkyl halide with alcoholic KOH gives alkene, but with aqueous KOH gives mainly:
explain: Aqueous KOH favours substitution (SN) to give the alcohol. Alcoholic KOH favours elimination.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Compared with trans-2-butene, cis-2-butene has a higher:

subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which alkene is NOT capable of showing cis-trans isomerism?
explain: In CH₃–C(CH₃)=CH–CH₃ one doubly bonded carbon has two identical CH₃ groups, so no geometrical isomerism.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Peroxide (Kharasch) effect, giving anti-Markovnikov addition to alkenes, is observed only with which HX?

prompt: Order of reactivity of hydrogen halides in electrophilic addition to alkenes?
explain: Acid strength and ease of H–X cleavage: HI > HBr > HCl > HF.

prompt: Major product of 3-methylbut-1-ene + HBr (no peroxide)?

subject: Chemistry

prompt: Order of heats of hydrogenation (ΔH, magnitude) of butene isomers?

subject: Chemistry

prompt: Alkene with Hg(OAc)₂/H₂O, then NaBH₄ gives alcohol by which pattern?

subject: Chemistry

prompt: Major product of CF₃–CH=CH₂ + HBr (no peroxide)?

prompt: Which reagent decolourises reddish-brown Br₂ in CCl₄ at once, as a test for the C=C bond?
explain: Alkenes add Br₂ rapidly to give a colourless vicinal dibromide; alkanes and benzene do not react in the dark.

prompt: Peroxide (Kharasch) effect is observed only with which halogen acid?

prompt: Why does HCl not show the peroxide effect with propene?
options: H–Cl bond too strong; H abstraction endothermic
Cl• is too stable to form
Cl• does not add to alkenes

prompt: In the peroxide effect on propene, which radical intermediate forms after Br• attack?

prompt: Hydration of propene with dil. H₂SO₄ gives mainly?

prompt: 2-Methylpropene + HBr in the presence of peroxide gives?

prompt: Which alkene gives the same product with HBr whether or not peroxide is present?

prompt: Addition of one mole HBr to propyne gives mainly?
explain: The Markovnikov product is CH₃C(Br)=CH₂. Excess HBr then gives 2,2-dibromopropane.

prompt: Product of vinyl chloride with HCl (Markovnikov)?

prompt: HBr adds to CF₃CH=CH₂ to give mainly?

prompt: Rate-determining step in electrophilic addition of HX to an alkene?
options: Attack of X⁻ on the carbocation
Loss of H⁺ from the product

prompt: Propene + HOCl gives mainly?
explain: Cl⁺ (electrophile) goes to the carbon with more H, and OH to the more substituted carbon, giving 1-chloropropan-2-ol.

prompt: HBr adds to 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene mainly giving which product?

prompt: Which pair of steps forms the propagation steps of the HBr peroxide addition?
options: Br• adds to alkene; radical abstracts H from HBr
Br₂ forms; Br₂ adds to alkene
H• adds to alkene; Br• abstracts H
R–O• adds to alkene; Br⁻ attacks
explain: The alkyl radical formed from Br• addition abstracts H from HBr, giving the product and regenerating Br•.

prompt: Why does HI not show the peroxide effect with propene?
options: I• is too unreactive to add to C=C
H–I bond is too strong to cleave
I• adds only to give a 1° carbocation

prompt: Ozonolysis of an alkene: which reagent pair gives aldehydes/ketones without over-oxidation?

prompt: Ozonolysis with oxidative workup (H₂O₂): an aldehyde fragment is converted to a…
explain: H₂O₂ oxidises RCHO to RCOOH; ketones remain unchanged.

prompt: Order of intermediates in ozonolysis of an alkene:
explain: Primary ozonide (molozonide) is unstable and rearranges to the secondary ozonide.

prompt: Ozonolysis of propene (reductive workup) gives?
explain: CH₂= gives HCHO; CH₃CH= gives CH₃CHO.

prompt: Ozonolysis of 2-methylpropene (reductive) gives?
explain: (CH₃)₂C= gives acetone; CH₂= gives HCHO.

prompt: Ozonolysis of 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene gives?

prompt: Ozonolysis of cyclohexene (reductive workup) gives?

prompt: Ozonolysis of benzene followed by Zn/H₂O gives how many moles of glyoxal per mole?

prompt: Main synthetic use of ozonolysis in structure determination of alkenes:
options: Count the number of H atoms
Locate the position of the C=C bond

prompt: Role of Zn dust in the reductive workup of ozonide:

prompt: Alkene C₅H₁₀ giving HCHO and butanone on reductive ozonolysis is?

prompt: Ozonolysis of 2-methylbut-2-ene (reductive) gives?

prompt: Ozonolysis of styrene (C₆H₅CH=CH₂), reductive workup, gives?

prompt: Ozonolysis of but-1-ene (reductive) gives?

prompt: Propene ozonolysis with H₂O₂ workup gives ethanoic acid and which other product?

prompt: Typical conditions for ozonolysis step with O₃:
options: Low temp (≈ −78 °C), inert solvent like CH₂Cl₂

prompt: The cyclic ozonide formed in ozonolysis of an alkene is a:

prompt: Ozonolysis of 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene (reductive workup) gives?

prompt: Ethyne passed through a red-hot iron tube at 873 K mainly gives which product?

prompt: Cyclic trimerisation of propyne (CH₃–C≡CH) gives which compound?

prompt: Ethyne reacts with Ni(CN)₂ at high pressure, and four units join to form:

prompt: Low-density polythene is made from ethene by which type of mechanism?

prompt: High-density polythene is prepared from ethene using which catalyst?

prompt: Which monomer gives Teflon on polymerisation?

prompt: Polyacrylonitrile (orlon) is formed by addition polymerisation of:

prompt: Ethyne polymerised with a Ziegler–Natta catalyst gives a polymer with which special property?
explain: Polyacetylene has conjugated double bonds and becomes a conducting polymer on doping.

prompt: Hybridisation of each carbon in ethyne changes to what when it trimerises to benzene?
explain: Each linear sp carbon of ethyne becomes a trigonal sp² carbon in the benzene ring.

prompt: Industrial/lab preparation of ethyne: CaC₂ + 2H₂O gives ethyne and which other product?

prompt: Vicinal dihalide on heating with alc. KOH (excess, then NaNH₂) mainly gives?

prompt: Which reagent converts 1,2-dibromoethane to ethyne most effectively?

prompt: Higher alkyne synthesis: RC≡C⁻Na⁺ reacts with R'X. Best choice of R'X?

prompt: Kolbe electrolysis of aq. potassium maleate/fumarate gives which hydrocarbon at anode?

prompt: Which gas does the ammoniacal Cu₂Cl₂ test with terminal alkyne give as precipitate color?
explain: Terminal alkynes give red precipitate of copper alkynide with ammoniacal Cu₂Cl₂.

prompt: Hydration of ethyne with dil. H₂SO₄/HgSO₄ gives which final product?

prompt: Every C–C bond length in benzene is about:

prompt: Average C–C bond order in benzene is:

prompt: Total number of σ bonds in a benzene molecule is:

prompt: Cyclooctatetraene is non-aromatic mainly because it is:

prompt: In pyridine, the lone pair on nitrogen lies in:
options: A p orbital, part of the π sextet
An sp² orbital in the ring plane
An sp³ orbital above the plane

prompt: In pyrrole, the nitrogen contributes how many electrons to the aromatic π sextet?

prompt: The cyclopropenyl cation (C₃H₃⁺) is:
explain: It is planar and cyclic with 2π e⁻ (4n+2, n = 0), so it is aromatic.

prompt: Number of π electrons in naphthalene is:

prompt: Actual heat of hydrogenation of benzene compared with 3 × that of cyclohexene is:

prompt: Resonance energy of benzene is approximately:
explain: Resonance energy ≈ 150 kJ/mol (≈36 kcal/mol).

prompt: Different resonance structures of a molecule differ in the:

prompt: The cyclooctatetraene dianion (C₈H₈²⁻) is aromatic because it is planar with:
explain: Adding 2 e⁻ gives 10π e⁻ (4n+2, n = 2), so the ring becomes planar and aromatic.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Why does benzene give only one 1,2-dibromo derivative, as Kekulé proposed?
options: Fixed alternate single and double bonds
explain: Kekulé suggested the double bonds oscillate, so the two 1,2-isomers interconvert and are one compound.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Order of stability for cyclic conjugated systems of similar size is:
explain: Aromaticity stabilises; anti-aromaticity destabilises relative to a non-aromatic analogue.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In nitrating mixture, the role of H₂SO₄ is to?
options: Act as a dehydrating agent only for benzene
explain: H₂SO₄ is the stronger acid; it protonates HNO₃, which loses H₂O to give NO₂⁺.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Further nitration of nitrobenzene (conc. HNO₃/H₂SO₄, heat) gives mainly?
explain: –NO₂ is a deactivating, meta-directing group, so the second NO₂ enters the meta position.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Direct iodination of benzene with I₂ needs which added reagent?
explain: I₂ is weakly electrophilic and HI formed is reversible; HNO₃ oxidises HI/I₂ to I⁺ and drives the reaction.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Benzene + excess Cl₂ in bright sunlight (no Lewis acid) gives?
explain: Under UV/sunlight, free-radical addition gives C₆H₆Cl₆ (gammexane), not substitution.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Phenol on treatment with conc. HNO₃ finally gives?
explain: –OH strongly activates o/p positions; conc. HNO₃ nitrates all three, giving picric acid.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Direct nitration of aniline with HNO₃/H₂SO₄ gives a considerable amount of which product?
explain: In strong acid, –NH₂ becomes –NH₃⁺, a meta director, so m-nitroaniline forms along with o/p.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Halogen substituent (–Cl) on benzene ring in EAS is?
explain: –I effect deactivates the ring, but +M lone-pair donation stabilises o/p σ-complexes.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Benzene + n-propyl chloride/AlCl₃ gives mainly which product?
explain: 1° carbocation rearranges (1,2-H shift) to more stable 2° isopropyl cation.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which feature of Friedel-Crafts acylation is absent in alkylation?
explain: Acylium ion (RC≡O⁺) is resonance stabilised, so it does not rearrange.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Why is Friedel-Crafts acylation product not further acylated?
explain: –COR is electron-withdrawing (–M), deactivating the ring; alkylation products are activated.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Friedel-Crafts reaction fails with which substrate?
explain: Strongly deactivated rings (–NO₂, –COR, –CN, –SO₃H) do not undergo Friedel-Crafts.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Why does aniline fail to undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction?
explain: Basic N-lone pair attacks Lewis acid AlCl₃, giving a strongly deactivated ammonium-type salt.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: The electrophile in Friedel-Crafts acylation with RCOCl/AlCl₃ is?
explain: AlCl₃ abstracts Cl⁻ from RCOCl to form the acylium ion.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Benzene + CH₃COCl/anhyd. AlCl₃ gives?
explain: Acylation introduces –COCH₃, forming C₆H₅COCH₃.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Benzene + benzoyl chloride/anhyd. AlCl₃ gives?
explain: C₆H₅COCl gives C₆H₅COC₆H₅ (benzophenone).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Benzene + (CH₃)₃CCl/AlCl₃ gives which product?
explain: 3° carbocation is stable and attacks directly with no rearrangement.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which reagent can replace acyl chloride in Friedel-Crafts acylation?
explain: Acid anhydrides with AlCl₃ also generate the acylium ion.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Nitration of aniline in strongly acidic medium gives mainly which product?
explain: –NH₂ is protonated to –NH₃⁺, a meta-directing group, so substantial meta product forms.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which group is a meta director owing to –I and –M effects?
explain: –CHO withdraws electrons by –I and –M, deactivating ring and directing meta.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Why are halogens o/p directing yet deactivating in EAS?
explain: –I lowers ring reactivity; +M lone-pair donation stabilises o/p arenium ions.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which is the strongest activating group for EAS in benzene?
explain: –NH₂ has strong +M; acylation of N or O reduces its lone pair donation.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Acetylation of –NH₂ in aniline (to acetanilide) does what to activation?
explain: N lone pair is delocalised onto C=O, so +M is weaker; –NHCOCH₃ is still o/p.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which is a meta-directing group?
explain: –CCl₃ has strong –I from three Cl atoms with no +M/hyperconjugation, so it is meta directing.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Nitration of nitrobenzene gives mainly which product?
explain: –NO₂ is meta directing; harsher conditions are required due to deactivation.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which group is o/p directing and activates the ring through +M effect?
explain: –OCH₃ donates an O lone pair into the ring (+M); the others are meta directors.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which pair contains only meta directors?
explain: –COOH and –CN are –M/–I groups, meta directing, deactivating.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Most reactive towards nitration among these?
explain: Toluene (+I, hyperconjugation) is activated; the others are equal or deactivated.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Least reactive towards EAS among these?
explain: –NO₂ is the strongest deactivator listed (–I, –M, strongest withdrawal).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Nitration of chlorobenzene gives mainly which isomer?
explain: –Cl is o/p directing; para is major due to less steric hindrance and –I effect at ortho.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which group is deactivating yet o/p directing?
explain: Halogens (–I) deactivate by –I but direct o/p via +M lone pairs.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which group is both activating and ortho/para directing but via –NHCOCH₃-type resonance?
explain: –NHCOCH₃ has N lone pair (+M), activating o/p; others are meta directors.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Why does nitrobenzene fail to undergo Friedel–Crafts alkylation or acylation?
options: Ring strongly deactivated by –M and –I of –NO₂
–NO₂ is an ortho/para director blocking attack
Steric hindrance by –NO₂ at all positions
explain: –NO₂ withdraws electrons by –M and –I, so the ring is too deactivated for the weak carbocation/acylium electrophile.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Decarboxylation of RCOONa with soda lime gives an alkane with how many carbons relative to the acid?
explain: Soda lime removes CO₂ as Na₂CO₃, so the alkane has one carbon less than the acid salt.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In Kolbe electrolysis of aqueous sodium acetate, which gas is liberated at the cathode?
explain: Alkane and CO₂ form at the anode; water is reduced at the cathode to give H₂ and OH⁻.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Br₂/CCl₄ adds to cis-but-2-ene. Which product forms?
explain: Anti addition of Br₂ to the cis alkene gives (2R,3R) + (2S,3S), a racemic mixture. The trans alkene gives meso.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Electrophilic addition: H2, X2, H2O, HX

prompt: Major product of 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene with dil. H₂SO₄/H₂O?
explain: The 2° carbocation undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift to give a 3° carbocation, which is trapped by water to give 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Electrophilic addition: H2, X2, H2O, HX

prompt: Which monomer gives PVC on addition polymerisation?
explain: PVC (polyvinyl chloride) is formed from vinyl chloride, CH₂=CHCl.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Polystyrene is obtained by polymerisation of which monomer?
explain: Styrene (vinylbenzene), C₆H₅CH=CH₂, undergoes addition polymerisation to polystyrene.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In Hg²⁺/H₂SO₄ hydration of an alkyne, the unstable first-formed intermediate is a(n)?
explain: Markovnikov addition of water gives a vinyl alcohol (enol), which tautomerises to the more stable carbonyl compound.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Alkynes: addition of H2, X2, H2O, HX

prompt: Alkynes add electrophiles (Br₂, HX) more slowly than alkenes mainly because the intermediate formed is a:
explain: Electrophilic attack on an alkyne gives a high-energy vinyl cation (sp C), so alkynes are less reactive than alkenes.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Alkynes: addition of H2, X2, H2O, HX

prompt: Bromine water with phenol at room temperature gives mainly which product?
explain: –OH strongly activates the o/p positions, so all three are brominated; white ppt of 2,4,6-tribromophenol.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which substituent on benzene is a meta director in EAS?
explain: The positively charged N has a strong –I effect and no lone pair, so it deactivates the ring and directs meta.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Wolff–Kishner reduction converts C=O to CH₂ using which reagent?
explain: Wolff–Kishner uses hydrazine and KOH (basic medium); Clemmensen is the acidic Zn–Hg/HCl method.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Hydrolysis of aluminium carbide, Al₄C₃, with water gives which alkane?
explain: Al₄C₃ contains C⁴⁻ (methanide) ions, which on hydrolysis give CH₄.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: 1,4-Dibromobutane heated with Na in dry ether mainly gives:
explain: Intramolecular Wurtz coupling of an α,ω-dihalide forms a cycloalkane (a four-membered ring here).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In soda lime (NaOH + CaO), what is the main role of CaO?
options: Supplies the carbon for the alkane
Keeps NaOH dry and less corrosive to glass
Acts as the catalyst for decarboxylation
explain: CaO prevents NaOH from absorbing moisture (it is deliquescent) and lowers its attack on glass; it also raises the fusion point.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Rate of dehydrohalogenation of R–X with alc. KOH to give alkene follows which order?
explain: Weaker C–X bond leaves more easily, so C–I breaks fastest and C–F slowest.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: For E2 dehydrohalogenation, the β-H and the leaving halogen must preferably be:
explain: E2 is a concerted anti elimination, with H and X in the same plane at 180°.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Compared with cis-but-2-ene, trans-but-2-ene has a higher:
explain: Trans is symmetrical and packs better in the crystal lattice, so it melts higher. Cis has the higher μ and b.p.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Heating butan-1-ol with conc. H₂SO₄ gives mainly which alkene?
explain: 1° carbocation shifts hydride to give 2° carbocation, then Saytzeff elimination gives but-2-ene.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Stereochemistry of H₂ addition to an alkene over Pd/C or Pt surface?
explain: Both H atoms are delivered from the catalyst surface to the same face of the C=C, so addition is syn.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Electrophilic addition: H2, X2, H2O, HX

prompt: Cyclohexene + Br₂ in CCl₄ gives mainly which product?
explain: Anti opening of the bromonium ion by Br⁻ gives trans-1,2-dibromocyclohexane (racemic).
subject: Chemistry
topic: Electrophilic addition: H2, X2, H2O, HX

prompt: Styrene (C₆H₅CH=CH₂) + HBr, no peroxide, gives mainly?
explain: H adds to CH₂; the benzylic carbocation, stabilised by resonance, gives PhCH(Br)CH₃.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: 1-Methylcyclohexene + HBr (no peroxide) gives mainly?
explain: H adds to the C with more H (C-2), forming a 3° carbocation at C-1; Br⁻ then attacks it.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In the peroxide effect, which radical abstracts H from HBr in the initiation step?
explain: Peroxide homolysis gives RO•, which abstracts H from HBr to generate Br•.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Order of stability of alkyl free radicals (relevant to the peroxide effect)?
explain: Hyperconjugation stabilises radicals as it does carbocations, so more alkyl groups mean a more stable radical.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: The six π electrons of benzene are best described as:
options: Held by alternate carbon atoms only
explain: Six p orbitals overlap sideways to give a delocalised π cloud above and below the ring plane.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which of these is aromatic?
explain: C₃H₃⁺ is cyclic, planar, fully conjugated with 2π e⁻ (4n+2, n=0). C₅H₅⁺ and C₇H₇⁻ have 4 and 8 π e⁻.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Phenol reacts with dilute HNO₃ at 298 K. What is obtained?
explain: The strongly activating –OH directs o/p; dilute HNO₃ gives o- and p-nitrophenol, while conc. HNO₃ gives picric acid.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In EAS of nitrobenzene, o/p attack is disfavoured because the σ-complex has +ve charge on?
explain: o/p attack puts + charge on the C attached to –NO₂, which is very unstable; meta attack avoids this.
subject: Chemistry
